It recreates the general structure, flows, and interactions of a trading-platform interface (onboarding, landing, demo trade lookup, subscription packages, countdown, demo payment) with zero real functionality: no real money, no payment providers, no real financial transactions — every balance, trade, profit, and customer is visibly mock data. A persistent "DEMO PLATFORM — NOT A REAL FINANCIAL SERVICE" banner stays visible at the top at all times.
    Audience & RolesGeneral visitors exploring a demonstration interface. Single public audience, no accounts, no roles, no login — anyone who opens the site goes through the same onboarding and demo flows. All data is local mock data; nothing is user-specific or persisted beyond the browser.
    Core FlowsThese flows must work end-to-end:Visitor arrives → sees persistent demo disclaimer banner → onboarding/welcome screen with PLATFORM XM branding, short explanation of how the demo works, Continue and Skip buttons → lands on main dashboardVisitor browses landing page: hero, animated statistics (30,000 accounts / 50,000 trades / 7,800,000 ج.م profit), demo customer results cards, about section — smooth-scroll navigation with mobile hamburger menuVisitor opens subscription modal → enters full name and demo receiving number → selects a fictional package (750→4,150 / 1,000→6,500 / 2,300→10,500 / 3,200→19,000 / 5,000→33,000 / 6,500→52,000 / 8,000→65,000 ج.م, all labeled DEMO VALUES) → a demo trade ID like XM-DEMO-482931 is generated → success state with Copy ID, View Demo Trade, Return to dashboardVisitor enters a trade/account number in the search section → mock trade details render: name, investment, demo profit, receiving number, payment status, remaining time, deposit amount, trade ID — all in Egyptian Pound and marked as demo dataVisitor views a demo trade → live countdown (hours/minutes/seconds) runs → at zero shows a simulated expired stateVisitor clicks Simulate Payment in the demo payment section (frontend-only, connected to nothing) → trade status changes to 'Demo payment completed' with a success notification — no real payment occursCopy-to-clipboard for demo trade IDs, form validation with inline messages, toast notifications for all demo actions — everything works without a backend using local mock data
    Technical RequirementsBuilt on Base44's React + Tailwind stack (original React-free HTML/CSS/JS structure is replaced by React components, but behavior is identical: no backend, all data from local mock data/localStorage). All monetary values in Egyptian Pound (ج.م), never $/USD. Mock trade data stored client-side (in-memory + localStorage for created demo trades). Working JavaScript countdown with expired state. Copy-to-clipboard for trade IDs. Fully responsive on desktop/tablet/mobile with no horizontal overflow, working mobile menu and modals. Subtle animations only: fade-in, slide-up, hover transitions, counter animation, smooth scrolling.
    Design PreferencesCompletely original visual identity, not copying the reference site: very dark premium dashboard aesthetic — background #07090D, cards #0E1219, header/sidebar #0C0F14, borders #1C222C, neon lime-green primary accent, white primary text, gray secondary text. Premium, modern, minimal, dark, technical, professional. Strong hero with original copy and a supporting visual. Clean iconography, generous spacing, card-based sections for statistics, trade details, packages, and demo customer results.

    1. Architecture — React frontend (unchanged design) + Base44 platform backend: managed auth (registration, login, logout, password hashing, sessions, email verification), a real document database (entities), Row-Level Security for authorization, private file storage for screenshots, and serverless backend functions for order creation, proof submission, and admin review. README rewritten.

    4. Run the backend — Functions deploy automatically when saved; no separate server. Frontend: npm install then npm run dev (or npm run build).

    Upload never marks a payment paid — proofs stay Pending Verification until an admin approves them; approval/rejection and order-status changes automatically notify the user and write to the admin activity log.

    1. Backend technology

    10. Remaining production requirements

    Connect a licensed payment provider (e.g. Stripe) via its official API + signed webhooks so a real payment — not a screenshot — confirms an order; add KYC/AML and local financial licensing; transactional email to non-users needs a paid plan + verified custom domain.
